releaseNotes:
## Downloads

- macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon: signed, notarized and stapled Developer ID installer (`.pkg`).
- Windows 10/11, x64: unsigned NSIS installer (`.exe`) with optional NVIDIA CUDA support; installation is manual.
- **New: Linux x64.** Two `.deb` packages for Debian/Ubuntu amd64, built on Ubuntu 20.04 (glibc 2.31 or later):
  - `crossdesk-linux-amd64-v1.7.7-3-20261126.deb`: the standard package, uses the existing desktop session.
  - the `virtual-desktop-xfce` package: the same app, and APT also installs Xvfb, Xfce and the D-Bus session tools for hosts without a desktop.

  Install only one of the two with `sudo apt install ./<package>.deb`.
- Verify the downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Install this release manually once

This release signs the fork's update feed with a new key. **v1.7.7-1 and v1.7.7-2 only trust the old key**, so the in-app updater on those versions cannot verify the new feed and will not offer this update. Download and install v1.7.7-3 by hand once; later releases arrive in the app again.

## Changes

- Upstream CrossDesk changes since v1.7.7-2:
  - Device groups can be deleted; their devices and connection history are kept.
  - When launched at login, CrossDesk starts in the system tray by default (configurable), and older autostart settings are migrated on upgrade.
  - Connection history is kept separately for each signaling server.
  - Display-change fixes on macOS, Windows and Linux X11: privacy screens stay covered and the pointer stays aligned when displays are added, removed or woken from idle.
- English stays the default language for new installs. The Vietnamese translation is now complete and can be selected in Settings; installs that already saved a language keep it.
- The GitHub button in **Feedback & suggestions** has been removed, so diagnostic logs are never sent to a public issue tracker. Export the logs there and send the ZIP to your CrossDesk administrator.
- Update checks only report a new version when that release has a package for your platform, and large update downloads get 30 minutes again before timing out.
- First Linux build of CrossDesk Postcard. All three platforms are built from the same source commit by the fork's release pipeline, which checks every binary for the fork update channel and signaling defaults before publishing.
- Keeps Postcard, DeskHub and the fork update channel. The default signaling endpoint remains `crossdesk.ecom.io.vn:9099`.
